expectations.evidence: Part 1 'VIP Preview Night' is a ticketed experience ('40 tickets. $15, credited toward any purchase'), and the opener characterizes Cross's approach as 'a ticketed or limited "experience"', which matches the skill's core idea (ticketed in-store class). It omits Cross's specifics (the $47–$97 class, the free 14-day challenge, bring-a-friend/refer-two gifts) but the ticketed-event concept itself is used and nothing stated is wrong.

Part 2's 'Woolner-style teach → offer' is a generic paid $25 in-store workshop ending in a 15%-off offer. None of Woolner's distinctive funnel appears: the free lunch 'Reboot' workshop held at other businesses, booking through existing relationships, lead boxes, 'welcome guest' outreach, case value, or the Epic Event's 3 invites → RSVP → reminders → 'Glue and Offer' raffle. The response itself says 'I don't have the exact text of... Chad Woolner's chapters'. Generic workshop advice labeled as Woolner's.

expectations.text: Adapts both concretely to a vintage-furniture pop-up
expectations.evidence: Concrete vintage adaptations: theme nights ('Mid-Century Night'), sneak-peek hero pieces ('1962 teak credenza'), 'story card' on each piece, 'How to Spot, Score & Style Vintage Furniture' workshop, delivery partner logistics, 'Hunt List' sourcing service.

'Promotion timeline (3 weeks)' (Early Access List, list-first ticket release, $10–$20/day local ads, '12 tickets left' update, reminder texts) and Part 3 'Week +1: Thank-you email, "what sold" recap, unsold-piece flash sale to the list, review ask' plus ongoing 'Next Drop' list.
'Numbers to plan around': 40 VIP tickets × $15, 20 workshop seats × $25, 300–500 list sign-ups, 60–70% VIP conversion at avg $350, 150–300 public visitors at 15–25%, $200–$400 ad spend.
